mechanisms.decisive_claim: For every prime b and every sequence 0<epsilon_K<1/2 with epsilon_K^2 K tending to infinity, there is a support-minimal bad path on 2 floor(epsilon_K K/4)+1 vertices above N/b^(D_K+1), D_K=ceil(8/epsilon_K+1), avoiding every prescribed prime below b^floor((1/2-epsilon_K)K).
mechanisms.kill_test: Prove exact Bertrand, exponent-reserve, balancing, distinctness, and minimality bounds uniformly for the moving parameter.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The same parameterized construction works under the weaker hypothesis epsilon_K K tending to infinity.
mechanisms.kill_test: Take epsilon_K comparable to K^(-1/2) and compare the epsilon_K K padding reserve with the order 1/epsilon_K balancing decrement.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The moving-epsilon construction stays in one fixed multiplicative tail independent of epsilon_K even when epsilon_K tends to zero.
mechanisms.kill_test: Lower-bound the maximum balancing decrement when s_K is order epsilon_K K and epsilon_K tends to zero.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The path host can avoid every controlled prime up to N^(1/2+eta) for fixed eta>0 while all vertices remain at most N.
mechanisms.kill_test: Inspect an internal vertex incident to two edge primes both exceeding N^(1/2+eta).

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every o(N) deterministic uniform valuation-query tree whose finite all-zero branch omits b, queries primes below N^(1/2-epsilon), and has reciprocal mass at most 1-delta misses a support-minimal bad relation for all sufficiently large N=b^K.
mechanisms.kill_test: Force the zero leaf to retain by its delta N-t population, then construct a bad path avoiding exactly the primes on that adaptive branch.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For a shared-seed randomized uniform valuation-query tree satisfying the same seedwise zero-branch hypotheses, Pr(the output deletion is a transversal)<=E|D|/(delta N-t); hence expected o(N) cost has success probability o(1).
mechanisms.kill_test: Condition on the seed, prove success implies zero-leaf deletion, charge delta N-t vertices on that event, and take expectations.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The randomized success bound remains valid with no uniform lower bound on the seedwise all-zero population.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use zero branches querying growing initial prime sets whose coprime density tends to zero and delete that complete branch at o(N) cost.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The zero-branch theorem remains valid when the padding prime b is queried and receives valuation zero.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use b-adic product balance on unequal shores and inspect the positive, nonconstant padding valuations in the path construction.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The same no-go theorem holds when every integer is classified by its own hard-coded valuation-query program.
mechanisms.kill_test: Encode an exact target label into each program and delete one chosen vertex of every displayed path without a common zero transcript.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The zero-branch expectation bound also rules out a global post-classification alteration that may inspect missed bad supports.
mechanisms.kill_test: After a seedwise zero branch retains the constructed path, delete one of its vertices as a repair and test whether the original population charge applies.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Conditioning converts fresh independent query randomness for every input integer into one common deterministic tree covered by the shared-seed theorem.
mechanisms.kill_test: Condition on all per-input coins and check whether the resulting classifier is one uniform program or a different hard-coded program for each integer.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A seedwise adversarial relation is invalid because the bad support must be chosen before the random seed is sampled.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use the definition of a transversal, which must meet all hypergraph edges for each realized deletion set, and test whether an edge may witness failure after the set is fixed.
